newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on government measures.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on government measures.

text.p: The won reversed a long slump on Monday and ended higher against the U.S. dollar after the government announced measures to attract foreign hard currency inflows, dealers said.
The finance and economy ministry said it would speed up the domestic capital market liberalisation and expand overseas borrowings by state banks to stop a fall in the local currency.

In a further move, the government said it would raise the foreign stock holding ceiling to 23 percent from the current 20 percent starting May 1. The won closed at 895.00 after opening at 898.90. It touched a daily upper limit of 877.00.
"Longs rushed to sell dollars, believing the government measures showed a firm intention not to stand idle by the won's sharp depreciation," said a dealer at Commercial Bank of Korea.
But the won fell sligthly from its intra-day high on late dollar short-covering combined with a belief that the foreign funds would not flow in the near future, dealers said.
They said the steps would contribute to easing a recent speculative dollar buying spree. But they forecast the dollar to be supported at around the 890.00 level.
The won's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 894.00 against 897.10 today. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
